title: try-with-resources and Exception Suppression
learningObjectives: Use AutoCloseable resources in try-with-resources statements
Declare and safely close multiple resources in one statement
Explain why resources close in reverse declaration order
Inspect suppressed exceptions when resource cleanup also fails
Replace manual cleanup logic with structured resource management

understand.concept: try-with-resources closes AutoCloseable resources automatically, including when the body throws. Resources close in reverse declaration order. If both the body and close operation fail, the body exception remains primary and close failures are suppressed.
understand.whyItMatters: try-with-resources and Exception Suppression helps learners create Java applications that are easier to reason about, test and maintain. It connects core language knowledge with realistic programming tasks.

explain.narrative:
## Resource lifetime and AutoCloseable

Files, streams, readers, writers and other objects hold resources that should be released promptly. Java's `AutoCloseable` interface defines a `close()` method. A try-with-resources statement declares resources in its parentheses and closes them automatically when control leaves the block, whether the block finishes normally or throws.

## Resource declaration and closing order

A resource declared in try-with-resources must implement `AutoCloseable` (or `Closeable`). Multiple resources can be declared in one statement, separated by semicolons. Java closes them in reverse declaration order: the last resource declared is closed first. This is useful when one resource depends on another, such as a reader wrapping an input stream.

## Primary and suppressed exceptions

If the try body throws and a resource's `close()` also throws, Java preserves the body exception as primary. The close failure is attached as a suppressed exception and can be inspected with `getSuppressed()`. If the body succeeds but closing fails, the close exception itself is thrown.

## Prefer structured cleanup

Use try-with-resources instead of hand-written `finally` blocks for ordinary AutoCloseable resources. Keep resource creation inside the try statement when possible, handle or propagate checked exceptions, and avoid manually closing the same resource. Test normal completion, a body failure and a close failure.

examples.title: Core concept
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try (var in = new java.io.ByteArrayInputStream(new byte[]{65, 66})) { System.out.println((char) in.read()); } } }
examples.explanation: Uses try-with-resources with an AutoCloseable byte stream.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try (var writer = new java.io.StringWriter()) { writer.write("CodeSaathi"); System.out.println(writer.toString()); } } }
examples.explanation: Shows automatic resource closure for a writer.

examples.title: Edge case
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { class R implements AutoCloseable { public void close() { System.out.println("closed"); } } try (R r = new R()) { System.out.println("body"); } } }
examples.explanation: Shows that close runs after the try body.

examples.title: API behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { class R implements AutoCloseable { public void close() throws Exception { throw new Exception("close"); } } try (R r = new R()) { throw new Exception("body"); } catch (Exception ex) { System.out.println(ex.getMessage()); System.out.println(ex.getSuppressed()[0].getMessage()); } } }
examples.explanation: Shows that a body exception remains primary and a close failure is suppressed.

examples.title: Test and verify
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try (var one = new java.io.StringReader("one"); var two = new java.io.StringReader("two")) { System.out.println("" + (char) one.read() + (char) two.read()); } } }
examples.explanation: Declares multiple resources; they close automatically in reverse order.

practise.guidedTask: Create two AutoCloseable resources that print from close(). Confirm reverse close order when both are declared in one try-with-resources statement.
practise.independentTask: Create a resource whose close() throws while the try body also throws. Print the primary exception and each suppressed exception.
hints: Declare AutoCloseable resources in the try header so Java closes them on every exit path.
When multiple resources are declared, remember that they close in reverse declaration order.
If both the body and close fail, inspect getSuppressed() on the primary exception.
practise.challenge: Refactor a manually closed reader into try-with-resources. Test normal completion and an exception thrown while reading.

questions.prompt: Which interface is commonly used by resources in try-with-resources?
questions.explanation: AutoCloseable defines close(), allowing try-with-resources to release the resource automatically when the statement exits.

questions.prompt: In what order are multiple try-with-resources variables closed?
questions.explanation: Resources are closed in reverse declaration order so dependent wrappers are closed before the resources they wrap.

questions.prompt: If the try body throws and close also throws, which exception remains primary?
options: The exception from the try body
questions.answer: The exception from the try body
questions.explanation: When both the body and close fail, Java keeps the body exception as primary and records the close failure as suppressed.

questions.prompt: How can close-time failures be inspected when another exception is primary?
questions.explanation: Call getSuppressed() on the primary exception to inspect exceptions thrown while closing resources.

questions.prompt: Which is a key benefit of try-with-resources?
options: Resources are closed automatically on normal and exceptional exits
questions.answer: Resources are closed automatically on normal and exceptional exits
questions.explanation: Try-with-resources closes declared resources after normal completion and when an exception leaves the block.
